## Runtime and tools

This is the Codex edition of Our Silly Games. It needs a local project folder, a shell, Bun and a browser. In a chat without those capabilities, explain that the author should open the project in Codex desktop or Codex CLI; do not claim to have built or previewed a game.

Resolve the installed plugin root from this skill's actual file location: this file is at `<plugin-root>/codex/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`. # Start a game

You are helping an author make a browser game and publish it on Our Silly Games. Work in this order. Do not write game code until the creative brief is done.

## 1. Preflight

Run `bun --version`. The `osg` command and local dev server need **Bun 1.3 or newer** (not Node).

- Missing or older: tell the author the one-line install and ask before running it.
  - macOS or Linux: `curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash`
  - Windows (PowerShell): `powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1 | iex"`
  - then restart the terminal and re-check.
- Never use `npx -y` or any floating package to run the CLI. Always run the bundled copy: `bun "${OSG_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/osg.mjs" <command>`.
- This edition works in a local Codex desktop or CLI project, with shell access. Ordinary browser chat cannot run the local build and preview.

## 2. Creative brief first

Follow the `osg-design` skill now, before any code: hook, friend test, 30-second loop, failure state, one more go, screenshot moment, visual direction. Save the result as `DESIGN.md` in the project. If the author already has a clear brief, confirm it against the rubric and move on. For couch, party or motion ideas (steering, fishing, swinging, a hand of cards per player), mention that phones can be controllers (the `osg-pads` skill).

## 3. Scaffold

- Empty folder: run `bun "${OSG_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/osg.mjs" init`, then `bun install` (this fetches the SDK tarball from oursilly.games/sdk, no npm account or scope needed, and creates the lockfile with its integrity hash that the server build requires; keep it committed). If `bun install` cannot reach oursilly.games, say so plainly and retry later; do not swap in another source for `@osg/sdk`. Then restyle and rewrite the starter to match the brief; the starter is a placeholder, not a design.
- Existing project: read `osg.json` and `AGENTS.md` and continue.
- Read the `getting-started` doc (`read_doc` with slug `getting-started`) if you need the details.

## 4. Build, then check

- Running the game: you start it for the author exactly as the `osg-dev` skill says (in the background, then one sentence with the link to open), and you stop or restart it when they ask. Never give them shell commands, process ids or `kill`/`pkill`/`Ctrl+C` instructions; they should never need a terminal.
- SDK usage: `osg-sdk`. Local running and testing: `osg-dev`. Multiplayer, NPCs, scores: `osg-multiplayer`, `osg-npcs`, `osg-scores`. Art, sound, fonts: `osg-assets`.
- Rules that fail games: `osg-rules`. Keep every font, library and asset inside the project; no CDN, no network calls.
- For a whole first game, `get_playbook` with name `first-game` is the checklist.

## 5. Tell the author the timeline

When they submit (`$osg-publish`, when they are ready to publish), we build the source, run the game in a cloud browser, check the rules, and **publish immediately if it passes**. They get an **email in about 10-20 minutes**, and can close the window. A rejection email says exactly what to fix.

Submitting needs an Our Silly Games account; nothing before that does. Once the game first runs, offer to connect their account now so publishing is ready later. Only if they agree, help them connect the osg account MCP server through Codex’s sign-in prompt. If they prefer to wait, continue building; $osg-publish handles account setup when they are ready. Do not start a separate CLI login for this native MCP workflow.

## Never

Ask for or store passwords, tokens or API keys. Put secrets in the game. Submit on the author's behalf without their explicit request to publish.
